label: Currency
hint: Select display currency; no FX conversion
meaning: The currency used to label every monetary input and result.
why: Keeps all costs in one consistent unit so the estimate is readable.
entry: Choose the currency in which you have already expressed all costs. Linked Price Watch rates require USD. Convert every non-USD assumption separately before linking; the calculator never converts existing amounts.
source: Your budgeting currency and any currency conversions you have performed separately.
example: Choose INR when all prices, salaries and expenses have been entered in INR.
influence: Changes monetary labels only; it does not change the numerical estimate or perform an exchange-rate conversion.
mistake: Do not change the label and assume USD prices have been converted into another currency.
zero: Choose a supported currency; this field cannot be disabled.

label: Annual volume growth
hint: Growth in attempted task volume
meaning: The expected yearly increase in attempted tasks after Year 1.
why: A growing workload can change future operating costs and the number of successful outcomes.
entry: Enter a yearly percentage between 0 and 100. Use one assumption for both later years.
source: Workload forecasts, adoption plans or historical demand trends.
example: Enter 20 for an illustrative expectation of 20% annual workload growth.
influence: Affects later-year task volumes, usage-driven expenses and costs marked as scaling with volume.
mistake: This is growth in attempts, not an improvement in task quality or success rates.
zero: Enter 0 to keep annual attempted volume unchanged.

label: Annual operating cost inflation
hint: Annual increase in people, remediation and ongoing operating costs. Token price changes are set separately.
meaning: The expected yearly increase in people, rework and ongoing operating expenses.
why: Captures cost pressure beyond the amount of work performed.
entry: Enter a yearly percentage between 0 and 100 for the costs covered by this assumption.
source: Internal salary plans, vendor budgets and finance-approved operating assumptions.
example: Enter 5 for an illustrative yearly operating-cost increase of 5%.
influence: Affects later-year labor, rework, monthly operating expenses and enabled human-only costs. It does not change token rates or other per-attempt tool charges.
mistake: Do not use this field for token-price changes; those have a separate input.
zero: Enter 0 to hold the covered unit costs steady before any workload scaling.

label: Monthly attempted AI tasks
hint: Average attempted workflow tasks per month in Year 1, including failures.
meaning: The average number of AI workflow tasks started each month in Year 1.
why: Establishes the workload served by the proposed solution.
entry: Enter a nonnegative whole number of workflow attempts per month, including attempts that fail.
source: Workflow logs, business activity records or a measured pilot.
example: Enter 10000 for an illustrative workload of ten thousand attempted tasks per month.
influence: Affects annual task volumes, usage costs, review, rework and an enabled human-only comparison.
mistake: Define a task consistently. An attempt is not necessarily one API call; one workflow may make several calls.
zero: Enter 0 for a no-workload scenario. Fixed and upfront expenses can still remain.

label: First-pass completion rate
hint: Share of attempts successful before remediation
meaning: The share of attempted tasks completed successfully before remediation.
why: Distinguishes reliable initial outcomes from tasks needing extra work.
entry: Enter a measured percentage between 0 and 100 using a consistent quality standard.
source: Evaluation results, quality checks and production task outcomes.
example: Enter 90 if 90 out of every 100 attempted tasks meet the required standard initially.
influence: Affects first-pass outcomes, initial failures, rework expense and successful-task costs.
mistake: Do not count a task as first-pass successful if it required remediation to meet the standard.
zero: Enter 0 if no tasks succeed initially; 100 means no initial failures.

label: Failed-task recovery rate
hint: Share of initial failures recovered. Rework costs still cover every initial failure.
meaning: The share of initially failed tasks that become successful after remediation.
why: Accounts for useful outcomes recovered from initial failures.
entry: Enter a percentage between 0 and 100 of initially failed tasks, not of all attempts.
source: Remediation logs and post-rework quality checks.
example: Enter 80 if 80 out of every 100 initially failed tasks are eventually recovered.
influence: Changes recovered successes, unresolved failures and successful-task costs. It does not automatically reduce the rework budget.
mistake: Rework is charged on all initial failures, even those that remain unresolved. Recovery is not a cost-saving switch.
zero: Enter 0 if no initial failures are recovered; 100 means all are recovered.

label: Input tokens per attempt
hint: Average input tokens billed
meaning: The average billed input tokens used by one attempted workflow task.
why: Captures the input-side model usage associated with your workload.
entry: Enter a nonnegative whole-number average covering the calls within a task.
source: Provider usage logs and traces from representative workflows.
example: Enter 2000 for an illustrative average of two thousand billed input tokens per attempt.
influence: Affects model input expense and the overall cost estimate.
mistake: Do not measure just the user prompt if system messages, context or other calls are billed as part of the task. Avoid duplicating remediation usage included in rework. When linking Price Watch, this value must represent one billed request in a consistent tier. For multi-call workflows or mixed request sizes, use verified blended manual rates.
zero: Enter 0 if this scenario has no billed input-token usage.

label: Output tokens per attempt
hint: Average output tokens billed
meaning: The average billed output tokens generated for one attempted workflow task.
why: Captures the output-side model usage, which may have a different rate from input usage.
entry: Enter a nonnegative whole-number average across representative tasks.
source: Provider usage reports and workflow traces.
example: Enter 500 for an illustrative average of five hundred output tokens per attempt.
influence: Affects model output expense and the overall cost estimate.
mistake: Use billed usage for the chosen model and tier, not only the visible text length. Keep remediation usage consistent with rework scope. Linked Price Watch matching checks this count against the selected model output and context limits.
zero: Enter 0 if no output tokens are billed.

label: Input price per 1M tokens
hint: Illustrative and unverified. Enter the applicable provider rate in your scenario currency.
meaning: The price of one million billed input tokens for the selected pricing assumptions.
why: Turns input usage into an estimated model expense.
entry: Enter a nonnegative rate in the same currency as every other monetary input. Alternatively, apply a model from Price Watch to populate and link the matching rate.
source: Your provider's official pricing, contract or invoice, including the applicable tier.
example: Enter 2 for an illustrative rate of 2 currency units per million input tokens. This is not a verified quote.
influence: Affects input-model cost. The annual token-price assumption can change this rate in later years. For Moonshot models with required cache writes, the linked effective input rate includes those charges and is labeled accordingly.
mistake: Check billing tier, context bands and discounts. A single average rate may not represent every provider pricing rule. Linked rates are read-only until you switch to manual pricing.
zero: Enter 0 only if input usage is free for the scenario; record the reason in the pricing reference.

label: Output price per 1M tokens
hint: Illustrative and unverified. Enter the applicable provider rate in your scenario currency.
meaning: The price of one million billed output tokens for the selected pricing assumptions.
why: Keeps output pricing distinct from input pricing.
entry: Enter a nonnegative rate in your selected scenario currency. Applying a Price Watch model fills the matching published output rate automatically.
source: Official provider pricing, a contract or an invoice for the relevant model and tier.
example: Enter 10 for an illustrative rate of 10 currency units per million output tokens. This is not a verified quote.
influence: Affects output-model cost and later-year token expense.
mistake: Do not use the input-token price here unless the provider actually charges the same rate. Linked rates are read-only until you switch to manual pricing.
zero: Enter 0 only when output tokens carry no charge in the scenario.

label: Other API/tools cost per attempt
hint: Other variable API and tool charges
meaning: Other usage-based API or tool charges associated with one attempted task.
why: Includes workflow services beyond the model's input and output token bill.
entry: Enter an average nonnegative amount per attempt in your scenario currency.
source: Invoices for search, retrieval, document processing, external tools or other metered services.
example: Enter 0.01 for an illustrative additional tool expense of one hundredth of a currency unit per attempt.
influence: Affects recurring usage costs as attempted volume changes. Token-price changes and operating inflation do not alter this entered unit rate.
mistake: Keep monthly subscriptions in software and licenses. Do not repeat token charges or remediation expenses already included elsewhere.
zero: Enter 0 if there are no additional per-attempt tool charges.

label: Cloud infrastructure per month
hint: Base monthly cost at Year 1 volume
meaning: The monthly infrastructure expense supporting the workflow at Year 1 workload.
why: Accounts for hosting, compute, storage and supporting infrastructure beyond the API bill.
entry: Enter an average nonnegative monthly amount attributable to this workflow.
source: Cloud invoices, infrastructure budgets or an agreed share of shared services.
example: Enter 500 for an illustrative monthly infrastructure budget of 500 currency units.
influence: Affects recurring operating costs. Inflation applies in later years; the adjacent scaling choice determines whether volume growth also applies.
mistake: Do not include a provider's token bill twice. Allocate shared infrastructure consistently rather than assigning the whole company bill.
zero: Enter 0 if no separate infrastructure expense applies.

label: Cloud scales with volume?
hint: Choose whether this expense grows with task volume as well as inflation.
meaning: Whether infrastructure expense rises with task volume in addition to inflation.
why: Distinguishes a workload-dependent infrastructure budget from a stable one.
entry: Choose Yes if the infrastructure budget is expected to grow with demand; otherwise choose No.
source: Capacity plans, cloud usage trends and engineering estimates.
example: Choose Yes for a service where hosting resources grow with traffic; No for adequate fixed capacity over the modeled range.
influence: Changes later-year infrastructure expense. It does not affect Year 1 infrastructure cost.
mistake: Scaling here assumes a smooth relationship with demand; stepped capacity purchases or volume discounts are not modeled separately.
zero: No removes workload scaling for this expense, but operating inflation still applies.

label: Monitoring & security per month
hint: Base monthly cost
meaning: The ongoing monthly cost of observing and protecting the workflow.
why: Includes the operational visibility and security needed to run the service.
entry: Enter an average nonnegative monthly monitoring and security amount.
source: Observability invoices, security-tool costs and operating budgets.
example: Enter 200 for an illustrative recurring budget of 200 currency units per month.
influence: Adds ongoing monitoring and security expense, with later-year inflation and optional demand scaling.
mistake: Keep initial security assessments and setup in one-time security and compliance; avoid duplicating general software licenses.
zero: Enter 0 if no separate recurring monitoring or security expense applies.

label: Monitoring scales with volume?
hint: Choose whether this expense grows with task volume as well as inflation.
meaning: Whether recurring monitoring and security expense grows with attempted volume.
why: Allows usage-priced logging or security services to respond to workload growth.
entry: Choose Yes for demand-sensitive costs, or No for a stable subscription or budget.
source: Vendor billing terms and expected log, trace or event volumes.
example: Choose Yes for monitoring billed by growing event volume; No for a fixed plan with adequate capacity.
influence: Changes later-year monitoring expense in addition to operating inflation.
mistake: Do not select Yes simply because the service is important; base the choice on how its cost changes with demand.
zero: No keeps workload growth out of this expense; inflation still applies.

label: Software & licenses per month
hint: Base monthly cost
meaning: The monthly cost of software subscriptions and licenses used by the workflow.
why: Captures recurring software expenses outside separately entered API and infrastructure costs.
entry: Enter an average nonnegative monthly amount attributable to the workflow.
source: License inventories, subscription invoices and procurement records.
example: Enter 300 for an illustrative software budget of 300 currency units per month.
influence: Adds recurring license expense with inflation and optional workload scaling.
mistake: Exclude subscriptions already included in monitoring, infrastructure or another expense category.
zero: Enter 0 if there are no separate software or license expenses.

label: Licenses scale with volume?
hint: Choose whether this expense grows with task volume as well as inflation.
meaning: Whether the software and license budget increases as workload grows.
why: Reflects additional seats, usage bands or licenses needed with increased demand.
entry: Choose Yes when the total budget is expected to grow with workload; otherwise choose No.
source: Contract terms, seat plans and procurement forecasts.
example: Choose No for an unchanged fixed subscription; Yes if workload growth requires a proportionately larger license budget.
influence: Changes later-year software expense; Year 1 remains the entered base amount.
mistake: License bands and seat counts can change in steps. This simple choice does not model individual contract tiers.
zero: No disables volume scaling only; operating inflation still applies.

label: Human review minutes per attempt
hint: Average review time across all attempts, including tasks with no review.
meaning: The average human review time allocated to every attempted workflow task.
why: Makes the people cost of checking AI work visible.
entry: Enter nonnegative average minutes across all attempts, including tasks receiving no review.
source: Time studies, sampled review queues and pilot observations.
example: If half the tasks need two minutes of routine review, enter 1 minute averaged across all attempts.
influence: Affects human-review operating expense and total ownership cost.
mistake: Keep incremental remediation time in rework if already budgeted there. Do not enter the time for reviewed tasks alone when only some tasks are reviewed.
zero: Enter 0 if the workflow has no routine human review.

label: Fully loaded reviewer hourly cost
hint: Labor cost including overhead
meaning: The fully loaded hourly cost of the people reviewing AI work.
why: Values review time using more than the base salary alone.
entry: Enter a nonnegative hourly amount in your scenario currency, including applicable employer overhead.
source: Finance-approved labor rates, staffing budgets or contractor rates.
example: Enter 30 for an illustrative fully loaded review rate of 30 currency units per hour.
influence: Affects review expense; the operating inflation assumption also affects later-year review costs.
mistake: Do not enter annual salary or add the same employer overhead again in another cost category.
zero: Enter 0 only when reviewer time is deliberately assigned no cost in this scenario.

label: Rework cost per initially failed task
hint: Cost incurred per failed attempt; recovery controlled separately
meaning: The incremental cost of handling one initially failed task, whether recovered or not.
why: Captures remediation effort that the normal task budget does not cover.
entry: Enter an average nonnegative amount per initial failure, covering the agreed scope of extra processing and human effort.
source: Remediation logs, retry usage, support records and observed task-level costs.
example: Enter 1.5 for an illustrative average remediation expense of 1.5 currency units per initially failed task.
influence: Affects recurring rework expense. Initial failure levels matter; recovery alone does not remove the charge.
mistake: Do not charge only unresolved failures. Avoid counting extra tokens or review here if those same costs are already included in routine usage or review.
zero: Enter 0 only if initial failures require no incremental remediation expense in the scenario.

label: Support & maintenance per month
hint: Base monthly operating support
meaning: The recurring monthly cost of keeping the workflow running and maintained.
why: Includes operational support, maintenance and incident handling outside other categories.
entry: Enter an average nonnegative monthly amount attributable to the workflow.
source: Support contracts, maintenance budgets and allocated engineering time.
example: Enter 1000 for an illustrative support budget of one thousand currency units per month.
influence: Adds ongoing support expense, with inflation and optional workload scaling.
mistake: Separate routine maintenance from initial implementation. Do not include routine review or per-failure remediation again.
zero: Enter 0 if no separate ongoing support expense is expected.

label: Support scales with volume?
hint: Choose whether this expense grows with task volume as well as inflation.
meaning: Whether the support and maintenance budget grows with attempted task volume.
why: Reflects a support burden that may increase as adoption expands.
entry: Choose Yes for a demand-dependent budget, or No for a stable recurring amount.
source: Support workload trends, service agreements and staffing plans.
example: Choose Yes if a growing workload needs proportionately more support; No if the existing service agreement covers the modeled demand.
influence: Changes later-year support expense in addition to operating inflation.
mistake: This is a simple workload-scaling assumption, not a detailed staffing or incident forecast.
zero: No removes workload scaling for support; inflation still applies.

label: One-time implementation
hint: One-time expense paid at the start of the project.
meaning: The one-time cost of designing, integrating and launching the workflow.
why: Recognizes the initial investment before routine operations begin.
entry: Enter a nonnegative project-start amount in the selected currency.
source: Implementation plans, vendor proposals and allocated delivery effort.
example: Enter 15000 for an illustrative initial implementation budget.
influence: Adds to initial investment and Year 1 total cost, not annual operating expense.
mistake: Do not repeat recurring maintenance, data preparation, training or compliance costs already entered in their own categories.
zero: Enter 0 if implementation requires no additional investment in the scenario.

label: One-time data preparation
hint: One-time expense paid at the start of the project.
meaning: The one-time cost of preparing the data needed to launch the workflow.
why: Captures initial collection, cleaning, labeling, migration or organization of data.
entry: Enter a nonnegative setup amount attributable to this workflow.
source: Data preparation plans, labeling quotes and project budgets.
example: Enter 5000 for an illustrative initial data-preparation budget.
influence: Adds to upfront investment and Year 1 total cost.
mistake: Do not repeat work already included in implementation. Ongoing data expenses belong in an appropriate recurring category.
zero: Enter 0 if the necessary data is ready and there is no additional setup cost.

label: One-time training & change
hint: Initial user training and change management, not ongoing support.
meaning: The one-time investment in user training and organizational adoption.
why: Recognizes that introducing the workflow can require more than technical deployment.
entry: Enter a nonnegative project-start budget for training and change activities.
source: Training plans, enablement budgets and change-management estimates.
example: Enter 3000 for an illustrative launch training and adoption budget.
influence: Adds to upfront investment and Year 1 total cost.
mistake: This means people training and change management. Do not interpret it automatically as model-training compute or duplicate ongoing support.
zero: Enter 0 if no additional training or adoption investment is needed.

label: One-time security & compliance
hint: One-time expense paid at the start of the project.
meaning: The one-time expense of security and compliance preparation for launch.
why: Accounts for initial assessments, controls and approval work.
entry: Enter a nonnegative upfront amount attributable to the proposed workflow.
source: Security reviews, audit estimates, compliance plans and vendor proposals.
example: Enter 2000 for an illustrative initial security and compliance budget.
influence: Adds to upfront investment and Year 1 total cost.
mistake: Keep ongoing security subscriptions in monitoring and security. This field does not automatically cover all future regulatory impacts.
zero: Enter 0 if no additional initial security or compliance work is required.

label: Operating contingency rate
hint: Applied to recurring operating costs
meaning: The reserve added to recurring operating expenses for uncertainty.
why: Provides an explicit allowance for operating costs that differ from the base assumptions.
entry: Enter a percentage between 0 and 100 based on the uncertainty you want to explore.
source: Finance policies, project risk assessments and operating experience.
example: Enter 10 for an illustrative operating contingency of 10%.
influence: Raises the operating-cost allowance. It does not add a reserve to one-time setup expenses.
mistake: Do not use this as a guarantee that every omitted cost is covered, or repeat a reserve already built into each expense.
zero: Enter 0 to show the operating estimate without an additional contingency allowance.

label: Annual discount rate
hint: Operating costs discounted at each year-end
meaning: The annual rate used to express future operating expenses in today's terms.
why: Helps compare costs occurring at different times on a consistent present-value basis.
entry: Enter a percentage between 0 and 100 appropriate to your scenario.
source: Your organization's finance team or approved investment-appraisal assumptions.
example: Enter 10 for an illustrative annual discount rate of 10%; this is not a recommended rate.
influence: Changes present-value results, not undiscounted totals, usage or initial setup expenses.
mistake: Do not confuse this with operating inflation or a provider discount. Upfront spending is paid at the start and is not discounted.
zero: Enter 0 when you want no reduction of future expenses for timing.

label: Human-only minutes per task
hint: Leave at 0 to keep the human-only comparison off. Enter measured manual time to enable it.
meaning: The time needed for a person to complete an equivalent task without the AI workflow.
why: Enables an optional comparison against a genuinely comparable human-only approach.
entry: Enter nonnegative average minutes per equivalent task. Leave at 0 to keep the comparison off.
source: Measured manual workflows and comparable quality checks.
example: Enter 10 for an illustrative manual task taking ten minutes, after checking equivalent scope and quality.
influence: Enables human-only costs and cost-advantage results. It never changes the AI workflow's own cost estimate.
mistake: A faster manual task is not comparable if the quality, scope or outcome differs. The comparison uses the same attempted workload.
zero: Enter 0 to disable the complete human-only comparison, even if other manual cost fields contain values.

label: Human-only hourly cost
hint: Optional baseline fully loaded cost
meaning: The fully loaded hourly labor cost for the human-only alternative.
why: Values the manual work independently of the AI-reviewer role.
entry: Enter a nonnegative hourly amount in the same currency as the AI scenario.
source: Finance-approved staffing rates or relevant contractor agreements.
example: Enter 30 for an illustrative manual labor rate of 30 currency units per hour.
influence: Affects human-only costs and cost advantages only when the comparison is enabled. It does not change AI costs.
mistake: Do not assume the manual worker and AI reviewer have the same rate unless that matches the workflow.
zero: Enter 0 only if manual labor is deliberately assigned no cost. This field has no effect while manual minutes remain 0.

label: Human-only overhead per task
hint: Optional baseline other direct cost per task
meaning: Other direct expenses incurred for each equivalent human-only task.
why: Includes manual-work costs beyond the fully loaded labor rate.
entry: Enter a nonnegative amount per task, excluding costs already in the hourly rate.
source: Manual-process budgets, consumables records and attributable service charges.
example: Enter 0.5 for an illustrative additional manual-task expense of half a currency unit.
influence: Affects enabled human-only costs and comparison results, not the AI estimate.
mistake: Do not add employer overhead again if the hourly rate already includes it. Only include costs attributable to the comparable manual task.
zero: Enter 0 when there are no additional direct manual-task expenses.

label: Annual token price change
hint: Optional yearly change in input/output token prices; 0% default; -20% is an illustrative scenario, not a forecast
meaning: The yearly change in input and output token prices after Year 1.
why: Lets you explore token-price uncertainty separately from general operating inflation.
entry: Enter a percentage greater than negative 100. Negative values represent price decreases; positive values represent increases.
source: A documented scenario assumption, contract schedule or pricing sensitivity analysis.
example: Enter -20 for an illustrative annual token-price decline of 20%. This is a scenario, not a forecast.
influence: Affects later-year input and output token expense only. It does not change other tools, workload or staffing costs.
mistake: Do not apply provider price expectations to every workflow expense, or treat an illustrative decline as guaranteed. Even with linked Price Watch prices, this remains your future scenario assumption; a current snapshot is not a three-year forecast.
zero: Enter 0 to hold token prices steady across all three years.

label: Pricing reference
hint: Add the provider, model, pricing link and date you checked the rates.
meaning: A note identifying the provider, model, pricing basis and date checked.
why: Makes the assumptions understandable when you revisit or share a scenario.
entry: Enter a short reference with the official pricing link, model, billing tier and verification date, using at most 2000 characters. Applying Price Watch records the model, billing scope, rates, fetch time and official source automatically.
source: Official pricing pages, your contract and the records used to verify the entered rates.
example: Example: provider and model name; standard tier; official pricing URL; checked on your chosen date.
influence: Adds context to saved scenarios. It does not verify prices, fetch live rates or change numerical results. Exported scenarios retain these rates and the reference; imports do not silently replace them with newer prices.
mistake: Do not label prices verified unless you actually checked the relevant source. Avoid placing private credentials or account details in this note.
zero: Leave a clear illustrative or unverified note when rates have not been checked; the field can also be left empty.
